label: DATA PROCUREMENT AND CORPUS GOVERNANCE. Not a research experiment. No representation run, no model scored, no hypothesis tested, no J3 outcome produced.
WHY_IT_STOPPED: the brief instructs that the disk report is informational UNLESS storage is plainly insufficient. It is plainly insufficient in both available locations, by a wide margin, so no download was started.

ARCHIVE_VERIFIED_AGAINST_THE_PRIMARY_SOU.method: queried the Zenodo REST API directly (https://zenodo.org/api/records/7708270) rather than relying on the brief's cited figures, which carried chatgpt.com source markers

ARCHIVE_CONTENT_INSPECTED_WITHOUT_FULL_D.method: ranged GET of the first 25 MB and a partial tar listing. 24 MB transferred. This was done to size the EXTRACTION requirement accurately rather than guess it.
ARCHIVE_CONTENT_INSPECTED_WITHOUT_FULL_D.implication_for_the_brief: the official train/validation/test assignment is carried by the directory structure, so PRESERVE THE OFFICIAL SPLITS needs no reconstruction - it is read directly
ARCHIVE_CONTENT_INSPECTED_WITHOUT_FULL_D.why_that_matters: FLAC is already compressed, so gzip achieves almost nothing on the bulk of the archive. Extracted size is therefore approximately equal to archive size, NOT smaller.

requirement.peak_for_the_brief_compliant_path: ~91 GiB - the brief requires verifying the archive hash BEFORE treating the corpus as authoritative, which means the archive must land on disk before extraction
requirement.stream_extract_alternative: ~45 GiB peak, but it makes archive hash verification impossible and is therefore NOT brief-compliant

users_mac_connected_folders.short_by: ~18 GiB for the archive, ~64 GiB for the compliant path

cloud_container.short_by: ~26 GiB for the archive, ~71 GiB for the compliant path
cloud_container.additional_objection: this container is EPHEMERAL and is reclaimed when the session ends, so a 45 GiB download here would be discarded even if it fitted

STORAGE_REPORT.verdict: PLAINLY INSUFFICIENT in every available location. The 1.9 TB volume on the Mac has only 29 GB free.
what_would_unblock_it: free approximately 100 GiB on the Mac volume, then acquire there
attach an external drive or NAS path and connect it as a session folder
acquire a subset rather than the full redux - Zenodo serves the whole archive as one file, so a subset needs a different distribution or a machine that can hold the whole archive once
acquire on a machine with space and mount or sync the extracted corpus
STORAGE_REPORT.recommended: the Mac, or storage attached to it. The corpus is a durable research asset and the cloud container is not a place to keep one.

PREPARATORY_WORK_COMPLETED_WHILE_BLOCKED.what: the consumed-content side of the freshness check, which needs only material already held

canonicalisation.velocity_excluded: velocity can differ between renders of the same music
canonicalisation.hash: SHA-256 of the deterministically sorted canonical serialisation

PREPARATORY_WORK_COMPLETED_WHILE_BLOCKED.stated_limitation: EXACT-content hash. It catches duplication, not similarity. Two renders differing by more than 1 ms in any note boundary hash differently. If the PM wants near-duplicate detection, that is a different tool and a separate decision.
PREPARATORY_WORK_COMPLETED_WHILE_BLOCKED.expected_self_test_when_the_corpus_arriv: BabySlakh is documented as a subset of Slakh2100, so these 20 fingerprints SHOULD match 20 Slakh2100 songs. If they do not, the fingerprint canonicalisation is wrong and must be fixed before any exclusion is trusted.

SEMANTIC_SUITABILITY_RECORDED_IN_ADVANCE.SYMBOLIC_DERIVED_ONLY: chord/root/tonal-centre labels derived from MIDI may be created later but must be labelled SYMBOLIC_DERIVED. They are not automatically perceptual ground truth.
SEMANTIC_SUITABILITY_RECORDED_IN_ADVANCE.PAD_HARMONIC_MEANING_GROUND_TRUTH: NOT_COVERED - Slakh does not settle whether a listener perceives a timbre-evolving but note-stable synth pad as undergoing meaningful harmonic change. That is the F1 target-semantic question and needs a separate fresh perceptual or controlled corpus.

FUTURE_PAD_SEMANTIC_CORPUS_REQUIREMENT_R.must_include: sustained pads and drones with gradual evolution, not only onset-driven material
FUTURE_PAD_SEMANTIC_CORPUS_REQUIREMENT_R.target_must_come_from: perceptual judgement or another independently defensible definition of musical change, NOT merely MIDI note occupancy
FUTURE_PAD_SEMANTIC_CORPUS_REQUIREMENT_R.status: THIS IS NEW EVIDENCE. Not created in MIR-CORPUS-01.

UPDATE_02.trigger: the Captain connected an external drive and freed space on the boot volume

STORAGE_NO_LONGER_THE_BLOCKER.why_the_external: the Captain's instruction, and it keeps ~91 GiB of transient archive and extraction off the boot volume

measured_throughput_to_zenodo.device_8_parallel_small_ranges: 0.87 MiB/s aggregate - the device link is the cap, not Zenodo

THE_NEW_BLOCKER_IS_TRANSFER_NOT_STORAGE.finding: Zenodo throttles whole-file and large-range transfers but serves SHORT ranges fast on first request. The burst figures were burst, not sustained - an ordered 128 MB chunked fetcher settled at 2.6 MiB/s, then stopped entirely.

RATE_LIMIT_TRIPPED.evidence: response headers carry x-ratelimit-limit: 133, x-ratelimit-remaining, x-ratelimit-reset and retry-after: 60. After the throughput probing, both endpoints began returning HTTP 206 with a zero-byte body at 0 B/s.
RATE_LIMIT_TRIPPED.cause: the analyst's own throughput probing - repeated parallel ranged requests in quick succession
RATE_LIMIT_TRIPPED.disclosed_because: it is the reason the first two download attempts stalled, and it is an operational fact worth carrying forward: Zenodo is a free public research host and must not be hammered
RATE_LIMIT_TRIPPED.remedy_applied: all probing and both download jobs stopped; a single-connection, long-backoff, resumable fetcher armed with a 600 s cooldown before it starts

THE_NEW_BLOCKER_IS_TRANSFER_NOT_STORAGE.realistic_eta: roughly 15 hours at ~0.9 MiB/s if the link holds, and the fetcher is resumable across interruptions and survives this session

WHAT_IS_RUNNING_NOW.design: ONE connection, curl -C - resume, --retry 5 --retry-delay 60, --speed-limit 2048 --speed-time 180, 120 s gap between attempts, up to 400 attempts, then md5 verification against 66a2301ed7b4d5f4f6d3383474e546c6
WHAT_IS_RUNNING_NOW.safe_to_rerun: yes - it resumes from whatever is already on disk
WHAT_IS_RUNNING_NOW.container_job_abandoned: the container's speed advantage evaporated once Zenodo settled, and the container is ephemeral. Once the archive is on the drive, extracting the metadata locally at 21.7 MB/s takes about 35 minutes.

GOVERNANCE_TOOLING_BUILT_AND_SELF_TESTED.scripts/corpus_fingerprint.py: extended - it now also captures Slakh's OWN provenance keys
GOVERNANCE_TOOLING_BUILT_AND_SELF_TESTED.scripts/corpus_manifest.py: new - builds the full corpus authority manifest

THE_IMPROVEMENT_THAT_MATTERS.discovery: every Slakh metadata.yaml carries UUID and lmd_midi_dir, naming the source Lakh MIDI Dataset file. BabySlakh carries them too.
THE_IMPROVEMENT_THAT_MATTERS.why_it_matters: that is the dataset's OWN identity key, and the known MIDI-duplication bug shows up directly as one UUID under several Track IDs. It is a stronger duplicate detector than a content hash.
THE_IMPROVEMENT_THAT_MATTERS.how_it_is_used: three keys, cross-checked rather than trusted individually - Track ID (insufficient alone, as the brief states), UUID/lmd_midi_dir (dataset provenance), and the independent symbolic content fingerprint. Any disagreement between the two independent keys is REPORTED as a finding, never silently resolved.

GOVERNANCE_TOOLING_BUILT_AND_SELF_TESTED.self_test_performed: corpus_manifest.py was run against the consumed BabySlakh tree using the consumed fingerprint record as its exclusion source. All 20 tracks were correctly classified EXCLUDED_CONSUMED_OR_DUPLICATE, which exercises the exclusion path end to end before the real corpus arrives.
GOVERNANCE_TOOLING_BUILT_AND_SELF_TESTED.time_to_produce_the_manifest_once_the_ar: about 35 minutes of extraction plus a few minutes of indexing
